text:
jules: quick question for the console team — when someone saves a per-route analytics view that includes a model pin and a routing hint, should the console load the view with the original routing semantics or always re-resolve against the current routing table?

rachel: my vote: re-resolve by default. folks expect saved views to reflect current infra. but we should persist the original routing hint as metadata for audits and reproducibility.

tom: re-resolving is safer for permissions/capacity mismatches, but we also need a clear UX for when the original config would have produced different results. maybe two modes: "Apply current routing" (default) and "Replay exact config" (advanced).

nora: +1. UI idea: small pill in the header that reads "replay: exact | active" — default is active. if a user chooses exact, we try to apply pinned routing and pinned model artifacts. If any pinned artifact is unavailable, show a banner with the reason and fallback used.

jules: That handles the UX. On the backend, how do we store it? I propose storing an optional expected_routing object in the saved view record (policy_id, model_hashes, region_hint). Null means nothing pinned. Also store real-time resolution decisions in a resolved_snapshot every time someone opens the view so telemetry/cost estimates are reproducible.

rachel: example DB fields: id, owner, scope (route|project|org), target_id, view_body_json, expected_routing_json (nullable), last_resolved_snapshot_id (nullable). snapshots table includes resolved_policy_id, resolved_model_hashes, timestamp, user_id.

tom: API contract sketch for saving a view: 

POST /api/console/views
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "name":"string",
  "scope":"route|project|org",
  "target_id":"route_123",
  "filters":[{"k":"string","op":"string","v":"string"}],
  "expected_routing": {"policy_id":"opt","model_hashes":["m:hash1"]}  // optional
}

Response 201 {"view_id":"v_456"}

nora: telemetry note: emit a console_view_evaluated event containing { view_id, mode:"active|exact", resolved_policy_id, resolved_model_hashes, cost_estimate_tokens, sampling_rate }. We need the resolved_policy_id when mode=active too (it indicates which policy the system chose at open time).

Example event: 

{
  "event":"console_view_evaluated",
  "view_id":"v_456",
  "user":"alice",
  "mode":"exact",
  "resolved_policy_id":"policy-dedicated-2",
  "resolved_model_hashes":["m:hash1"],
  "cost_estimate_tokens":1200,
  "sample_rate":0.01
}

jules: security/audit: expected_routing may contain model identifiers and policy ids that are sensitive. We need to ensure saved views appear in audit logs and are included in retention policies. SecOps wants the save event in the audit trail with who pinned what.

rachel: agreed. also add a permission check on pinning: only users with route-admin or policy-admin can pin an expected_routing.policy_id. Others can add model hints but not pin policies. If they attempt it, return 403.

tom: UX detail: when someone without permission opens a view with expected_routing, show a small inline note: "This view requested policy X — you don't have pin access, so we'll run in active mode. Click 'Replay exact' to request elevated access." clicking that can open an escalation flow or a request modal.

nora: and for SV (saved view) lists, show an icon when the view contains expected_routing. Hover tooltip: "Contains pinned routing or model artifacts — may produce different results when replayed."

jules: edge case: global scoped views that apply across multiple routes. We should allow per-target overrides: a global view can hold a list of per-route model hints. resolution should merge global filters with target-specific pins. We'll document merge rules (target pins override global pins).

rachel: implementationally, when evaluating a view across N targets we should batch-resolve policies and sample one representative snapshot per target for telemetry. beware N explosion — cap to first 50 routes unless user explicitly asks to expand.

tom: cost preview: the console should show two estimates: "Active estimate" (what will run today) and "Exact estimate" (what would have run at save time). Both numbers should include sampling metadata and be tied to the resolved_snapshot_id so they are reproducible.

nora: we should also add a small safety: if a pinned policy is expensive (e.g., Dedicated high-tier) and the current user would incur cost, show a red attention label before replaying exact.

infra-bot: Canary scheduled: views-routing-replay (canary-2) -> deploy window 2026-04-02T02:00:00Z.

jules: thanks infra-bot. Next steps: (1) I'll author the API contract and include audit requirements, (2) rachel will add telemetry schema entries, (3) nora will draft quick mocks for the header pill and list icon, (4) tom to add permission gating logic to the save endpoint. We'll sync in tomorrow's standup.

rachel: Figma link for quick mock: http://internal/figma/console-replay-pill

tom: ping me for the permission matrix, I'll drop a table in the design doc.

nora: ok wrapping up — this approach gives reproducibility without surprising people by default. :+1:

jules: perfect, thanks all.
